original_text: To the side of the terminal there will be controls for the user to select the feedback needed (see h.) This description applies to the terminals found in other modes. h) Terminal Controls: The terminal controls will allow the user to choose the feedback he or she wants to appear in the terminal.

attribute_scores.rationale: Phrases like 'To the side of the terminal' and 'feedback needed' are somewhat vague and lack precise interface specifications.
Lacks specific input options, default feedback states, error handling, and exact definition of 'other modes'.
Terminology aligns generally with the system context, though 'terminal' vs 'system' could be more precisely standardized.
Uses future tense ('there will be', 'will allow') instead of the mandatory normative modal verb 'shall' for the primary system action, and embeds a cross-reference parenthetical.
Technically realistic for a sensor-based gesture recognition terminal with feedback configuration.
Combines a requirement about the physical/interface placement of controls with a separate requirement description (h) regarding terminal control functionality across other modes.
Hard to verify objectively due to vague descriptions of control location and lack of explicit testable feedback options.

shortcomings.explanation: The requirement uses future tense ('will be') instead of the mandatory normative modal verb 'shall' required by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: To the side of the terminal there will be controls... h) Terminal Controls: The terminal controls will allow...
shortcomings.explanation: The requirement bundles the physical/layout requirement with a nested sub-clause (h) describing control functionality, violating the principle of singularity.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: see h) This description applies to the terminals found in other modes.
shortcomings.explanation: Relies on a vague cross-reference and an ambiguous external scope ('terminals found in other modes') without fully specifying the conditions or modes.

layer3.original_text: To the side of the terminal there will be controls for the user to select the feedback needed (see h.) This description applies to the terminals found in other modes. h) Terminal Controls: The terminal controls will allow the user to choose the feedback he or she wants to appear in the terminal.
layer3.refined_text: The FROG terminal shall provide controls to allow the user to choose the feedback to appear in the terminal.
changes_made: Replaced future-tense phrase 'there will be controls' with the mandatory normative modal 'shall provide controls' to comply with IEEE 29148.
Removed nested sub-clause notation ('see h.' and 'h) Terminal Controls:') to ensure singularity and eliminate internal structural redundancy.
Eliminated vague cross-references and ambiguous external scope ('terminals found in other modes') while retaining the core functional capability of the terminal controls.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The refined requirement preserves the exact functional intent of the original text—ensuring that terminal controls exist to allow users to select their desired feedback within the FROG system—while removing non-normative phrasing, structural violations, and vague cross-references.

checks.observations: The refinement successfully replaced future tense with the normative modal 'shall', eliminated the split/nested structure (DEF-2), and removed the vague cross-references and external mode dependencies (DEF-3).
No vague adjectives or subjective terms were introduced in the refined text.
The refinement does not invent physical layout details, specific UI protocols, or unstated technical mechanisms, remaining strictly within the original scope.
The core functional intent—that the terminal provides controls for the user to select feedback—is fully preserved.
The requirement adheres to IEEE 29148 syntax, utilizing the active voice and the mandatory modal verb 'shall'.

layer4.critique_and_feedback: The proposed refinement correctly addresses all identified defects while adhering strictly to IEEE 29148 syntax standards. It removes the non-normative future tense, eliminates the problematic structural bundling and nested sub-clauses, and strips away vague cross-references without altering the underlying functional intent of the terminal controls.
